Subject: POC plan & success criteria — FinLytics trial

Hi Emma / Raj —

Great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so we’re all aligned before the POC kickoff: 

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: Validate Redwood inference performance vs. current in-house endpoint for realtime risk-scoring (99th pct latency and cost targets).
- Primary datasets: anonymized transaction stream + historical batch for offline quality checks.
- Success criteria (customer-proposed):
  1) 95th pct latency <= 220ms on 2-token median prompt length under 30 TPS load.
  2) Model output parity: ROC-AUC delta <= 0.01 vs. baseline on holdout set.
  3) Cost target: <= 0.60x current per-token spend in POC config.

Proposed POC plan (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope, data access, and POC owner assignments.
- Week 1: Redwood will provision a dedicated trial instance, load model variant, and run initial smoke tests.
- Week 2: Run end-to-end throughput & latency tests + offline quality eval.
- Week 3: Iterate on config (batching/quantization) and produce results + review.

Ownership and asks from FinLytics:
- Provide anonymized sample dataset (S3 link) and a list of representative prompts by Fri 02/27. (owner: Raj)
- Approve security checklist (we’ll send SOC2 evidence) and open a short VPN/KV access window if needed.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf (POC outline), finlytics-eval-template.xlsx (evaluation template)

Can you confirm the success criteria above and the suggested timeline? Once you confirm we’ll lock in kickoff and Camila will send the formal MOP (mutual action plan).

Thanks —
Marissa

Quick technical checklist / pre-kickoff notes from SE: 

1) Access and network:
- Please confirm S3 path + IAM role or short-lived credentials. If FinLytics prefers we can accept a presigned S3 URL.
- If you need private connectivity, we’ll run a short VPN window; we’ll need an egress IP allowlist (please supply).

2) Test dataset and prompts:
- Send 3x representative prompt groups (short/medium/long) and a small holdout set (1000 records) for offline eval.

3) Baseline test harness:
- We’ll provide a small runner that produces latency percentiles and token counts. We recommend running at 1x, 5x, and 30x target throughput to observe tail behavior.

4) Observability hooks:
- Please enable a test route and let us know any rate limiting rules on your side to avoid skewed results.

I’ll be on the kickoff Wed 03/01 and will post a runbook in the Drive folder.

—Vivek
